svg.title: mm_tiled_1to1<2>: which thread loads which element
svg.text: mm_tiled_1to1<2>: which thread loads which element
toy N = 4, TILE = 2, block (bx = 1, by = 0), 2 × 2 threads; matmul_bench.cu:83–97

g.text: t = 0: thread (0,0) copies ONE element of A and ONE of B. Blue/green = the tiles this step needs.
step t = 0, thread (tx = 0, ty = 0) [1 of the block's 4 threads]
row = by·TILE + ty = 0·2 + 0 = 0 col = bx·TILE + tx = 1·2 + 0 = 2
aCol = t·TILE + tx = 0 bRow = t·TILE + ty = 0
t = 0: thread (1,0) copies ONE element of A and ONE of B. Blue/green = the tiles this step needs.
step t = 0, thread (tx = 1, ty = 0) [2 of the block's 4 threads]
row = by·TILE + ty = 0·2 + 0 = 0 col = bx·TILE + tx = 1·2 + 1 = 3
aCol = t·TILE + tx = 1 bRow = t·TILE + ty = 0
t = 0: thread (0,1) copies ONE element of A and ONE of B. Blue/green = the tiles this step needs.
step t = 0, thread (tx = 0, ty = 1) [3 of the block's 4 threads]
row = by·TILE + ty = 0·2 + 1 = 1 col = bx·TILE + tx = 1·2 + 0 = 2
aCol = t·TILE + tx = 0 bRow = t·TILE + ty = 1
t = 0: thread (1,1) copies ONE element of A and ONE of B. Blue/green = the tiles this step needs.
step t = 0, thread (tx = 1, ty = 1) [4 of the block's 4 threads]
row = by·TILE + ty = 0·2 + 1 = 1 col = bx·TILE + tx = 1·2 + 1 = 3
aCol = t·TILE + tx = 1 bRow = t·TILE + ty = 1
After the barrier of step t = 0: every thread reads cells that OTHER threads loaded. That is why cooperation needs a barrier.
line 93 __syncthreads(): all 4 cells of both tiles are written. Now thread (1,0) reads row 0 of sA and column 1 of sB:
sA[0][0] = 1 was loaded by thread (0,0); sB[1][1] = 0 by thread (1,1). Without the barrier it could read them before they exist.
k = 0: 1·1 = 1; k = 1: 2·0 = 0 → acc = 1. 8 HBM loads served 8 FMAs (2 per thread): each loaded float is used TILE = 2 times.
t = 1: thread (0,0) copies ONE element of A and ONE of B. Blue/green = the tiles this step needs.

After the barrier of step t = 1: every thread reads cells that OTHER threads loaded. That is why cooperation needs a barrier.
line 93 __syncthreads(): all 4 cells of both tiles are written. Now thread (1,0) reads row 0 of sA and column 1 of sB:
Whole block: 2 steps × 8 loads = 16 HBM floats for 4 outputs = 4 per output. Naive: 2N = 8 per output. Formula 2N / TILE = 4 ✓
